chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Uthman, from Abu Usama, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever hears a sneeze and praises Allah (Mighty and Majestic) and sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his Household, he will not complain of his eyes nor his teeth.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you hear it, say it, even if there is an ocean between you and him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward and etiquette for responding to a sneeze in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual act of responding to a sneeze with physical health, promising protection from eye and tooth ailments as a divine reward for gratitude. The emphasis on reciting the response even if separated by an ocean highlights the universality of this etiquette, transcending physical barriers to maintain communal spiritual connection. This reflects the Shia tradition of viewing mundane bodily functions as opportunities for dhikr and barakah.
